tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The quarterly report was clear, concise, and persuasive.
The proposal was both innovative and it reduced overhead.
Staff must clock in on time, finish assigned tasks, and following safety rules.
She enjoys analysing spreadsheets, drafting briefs, and to present findings.
The manager not only approved the budget but also extended the deadline.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Three adjectives sit in matching form, so the list is parallel.

Tip: When listing qualities, keep each item the same part of speech.

FALSE — "Both…and" joins an adjective to a full clause ("it reduced overhead").

Tip: Match structures after both…and: both innovative and cost-saving.

FALSE — The list shifts from bare infinitives (clock in, finish) to a participle (following).

Tip: After a shared modal, keep every verb in the same bare form: follow, not following.

FALSE — Two gerunds are paired with an infinitive ("to present").

Tip: Keep enjoy + -ing throughout: analysing, drafting, and presenting.

TRUE — "Not only…but also" links two matching past-tense verb phrases.

Tip: Place the same kind of phrase after each half of the correlative.
tasks.solution_overview: Read each sentence as a list or a paired construction. Ask whether every item shares the same grammatical shape. Correlatives such as both…and and not only…but also are correct only when the two sides match.

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Investors valued its stability, its growth potential, and its transparency.
The goal was to cut costs, improving morale, and increase output.
He is skilled at negotiating contracts but weak in managing teams.
The policy aims to protect consumers, encourage competition, and boosting innovation.
She likes reading market reports and writing executive summaries.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Three noun phrases share the same pattern with repeated "its."

Tip: Repeating a determiner can help keep noun lists visibly parallel.

FALSE — An infinitive series is broken by the gerund "improving."

Tip: After "to," keep bare infinitives: cut, improve, and increase.

TRUE — Adjective + preposition + gerund appears on both sides.

Tip: Parallel comparisons often reuse the same preposition pattern (at… / in…).

FALSE — The final item shifts from infinitives to a gerund ("boosting").

Tip: Finish the series with boost, not boosting.

TRUE — Two gerund phrases sit after "likes" in matching form.

Tip: Prefer reading… and writing… rather than mixing -ing with to-infinitives.
highlights: stability, its growth potential, and its transparency
tasks.solution_overview: Check lists of nouns, infinitives, and gerunds one item at a time. A single mismatched form is enough to mark the sentence false, even if the meaning is clear.

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The training covers how to operate the machine, how to log incidents, and how to report faults.
Candidates should be reliable, motivated, and have experience.
The firm both restructured its debt and renegotiated supplier terms.
Our priorities are recruiting talent, retaining clients, and to expand overseas.
The auditor asked whether the figures were complete, accurate, and timely.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Three "how to" infinitive clauses form a clean parallel series.

Tip: Repeating "how to" before each verb keeps the list balanced.

FALSE — Two adjectives are followed by a verb phrase ("have experience").

Tip: Use three adjectives (reliable, motivated, and experienced) or three verb phrases.

TRUE — "Both…and" joins two matching past-tense verb phrases.

Tip: Place the shared subject once, then keep both verbs in the same tense and form.

FALSE — Two gerunds collide with an infinitive ("to expand").

Tip: Keep gerunds throughout: recruiting, retaining, and expanding.

TRUE — Three adjectives modify the figures in matching form.

Tip: Short adjective lists are easiest when every item is a single adjective.
tasks.solution_overview: Watch for mixed categories: adjectives slipping into verb phrases, or gerunds mixed with infinitives. Correct parallelism keeps one pattern from the first item to the last.

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The launch was delayed by weak demand, rising costs, and because suppliers missed deadlines.
Either accept the revised offer or continue negotiating in good faith.
The brief must be short, focused, and without unnecessary jargon.
Neither the forecast nor the cash-flow model supports the expansion.
We need a plan that is realistic, affordable, and can be implemented quickly.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two noun phrases are followed by a because-clause.

Tip: Keep causes as nouns: weak demand, rising costs, and missed supplier deadlines.

TRUE — "Either…or" links two bare imperatives.

Tip: After either…or, use the same verb form on both sides.

FALSE — Two adjectives are followed by a prepositional phrase.

Tip: Prefer three adjectives: short, focused, and jargon-free.

TRUE — "Neither…nor" joins two noun subjects; the nearer singular noun takes a singular verb.

Tip: Parallel correlatives still need subject–verb agreement with the nearer noun.

FALSE — Two adjectives are followed by a modal clause ("can be implemented").

Tip: Stay with adjectives: realistic, affordable, and quick to implement.
tasks.solution_overview: Clauses and prepositional phrases often sneak into adjective or noun lists. If the first two items are adjectives or nouns, the third must be too.

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The committee decided to postpone the vote, to request further evidence, and that members should abstain.
Success depends on careful planning, disciplined execution, and continuous review.
The app is designed for browsing catalogues, placing orders, and to track deliveries.
She is responsible for preparing the slides and for presenting them to the board.
The memo was both poorly timed and written in an aggressive tone.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two infinitives are followed by a that-clause.

Tip: Keep infinitives: postpone, request, and ask members to abstain — or rewrite as three that-clauses.

TRUE — Three noun phrases follow "depends on" in matching form.

Tip: After a preposition, noun or gerund lists usually work best when every item matches.

FALSE — Two gerunds are paired with an infinitive ("to track").

Tip: Use tracking deliveries to keep the -ing series intact.

TRUE — "For" + gerund appears twice in matching form.

Tip: Repeating the preposition before each gerund makes the parallelism explicit.

FALSE — "Both…and" joins an adverb–adjective pair to a past-participial clause of different shape.

Tip: Prefer both poorly timed and aggressively written.
highlights: careful planning, disciplined execution, and continuous review
for preparing the slides and for presenting
tasks.solution_overview: Infinitive series and gerund series are easy to break with a stray that-clause or to-infinitive. Name the pattern of the first item, then force every later item to match it.

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The director wants employees who are punctual, who communicate clearly, and dedicated.
Not only did the firm cut headcount, but it also renegotiated leases.
Please submit the form online, attach supporting documents, and a covering letter.
The package includes flights, accommodation, and airport transfers.
He prefers to negotiate directly rather than relying on intermediaries.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two relative clauses are followed by a bare adjective.

Tip: Keep relative clauses throughout: who are punctual, who communicate clearly, and who are dedicated.

TRUE — Fronted "not only" uses inversion, and "but also" continues with a matching verb phrase.

Tip: After inverted not only…, keep but also + parallel predicate.

FALSE — Two imperatives are followed by a noun phrase.

Tip: Use three verbs: submit, attach, and include a covering letter.

TRUE — Three noun objects form a simple parallel list.

Tip: Ordinary product lists are correct when every item is a noun phrase.

FALSE — An infinitive ("to negotiate") is contrasted with a gerund ("relying").

Tip: Match forms: to negotiate… rather than to rely…, or negotiating… rather than relying…
tasks.solution_overview: Comparisons with rather than and lists that mix clauses with adjectives are frequent traps. Keep the grammatical category constant across the join.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The role involves reviewing contracts, advising clients, and attendance at hearings.
We are looking for someone who can think strategically, act decisively, and communicate persuasively.
The surplus will be used both to rebuild reserves and financing new projects.
Her strengths are attention to detail, calm under pressure, and solving problems creatively.
The board voted to approve the merger, to appoint an interim CEO, and to defer the dividend.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two gerunds are followed by a noun phrase ("attendance").

Tip: Use attending hearings to keep the gerund pattern.

TRUE — Three bare infinitives after "can" form a matching series.

Tip: Shared modals (can/must/should) demand the same bare verb form each time.

FALSE — "Both…and" joins an infinitive to a gerund.

Tip: Both to rebuild… and to finance…, or both rebuilding… and financing…

FALSE — Two noun phrases are followed by a gerund phrase.

Tip: Use creative problem-solving so all three items are nouns.

TRUE — Three infinitives after "voted to" stay in parallel.

Tip: Repeating "to" before each verb is optional but often clearer.
highlights: think strategically, act decisively, and communicate
both to rebuild reserves and financing
to approve the merger, to appoint
tasks.solution_overview: Job descriptions and board resolutions often hide mixed lists. Convert every item into the same type—gerund, infinitive, or noun—before you judge the sentence true.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The campaign was effective in raising awareness, in generating leads, and sales increased.
Applicants must either enclose a portfolio or they submit a link to an online gallery.
The analyst is known for rigorous methods, clear writing, and ethical judgement.
We aim not only to grow revenue but also market share.
The workshop taught participants to define objectives, to map stakeholders, and to draft a pilot plan.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two "in + gerund" phrases are followed by an independent clause.

Tip: Keep the preposition pattern: in raising…, in generating…, and in increasing sales.

FALSE — "Either…or" joins a bare infinitive to a full clause with a new subject.

Tip: Either enclose a portfolio or submit a link — same subject, same verb form.

TRUE — Three noun phrases follow "known for" in parallel.

Tip: After "for," noun lists are usually the safest parallel choice.

FALSE — "Not only…but also" joins an infinitive to a bare noun.

Tip: Not only to grow revenue but also to grow market share — or not only revenue but also market share.

TRUE — Three infinitives after "taught…to" match cleanly.

Tip: Repeat "to" when it keeps each learning outcome equally weighted.
highlights: rigorous methods, clear writing, and ethical judgement
to define objectives, to map stakeholders, and to draft
tasks.solution_overview: Correlatives fail when one side is a phrase and the other is a clause, or when one side has "to" and the other does not. Balance the two halves before you look at meaning.

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The tender requires bidders to demonstrate capacity, to provide references, and financial statements for three years.
Whether by email, by phone, or in person, clients must receive a reply within one working day.
The restructuring plan is ambitious, controversial, and it may fail.
She speaks fluently in English, in German, and Mandarin.
The software can schedule meetings, share files, and integrate with payroll systems.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two infinitives are followed by a noun phrase without "to provide."

Tip: Add to provide financial statements, or turn all three into nouns after "demonstrate."

TRUE — Three prepositional routes stay parallel after "whether."

Tip: Keep the same preposition pattern (by… / by… / in…) when listing channels.

FALSE — Two adjectives are followed by a clause.

Tip: Use three adjectives: ambitious, controversial, and risky.

FALSE — "In" appears before the first two languages but not the third.

Tip: Repeat in before Mandarin, or drop in before all three.

TRUE — Three bare infinitives after "can" form a matching list.

Tip: Shared auxiliaries make parallel verb lists especially clear.
highlights: by email, by phone, or in person
schedule meetings, share files, and integrate
tasks.solution_overview: Missing repeated prepositions and trailing clauses after adjective pairs are subtler errors. Read the list aloud; an abrupt change of rhythm usually signals a break in form.

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The CFO argued that costs were rising, that margins were shrinking, and cash was scarce.
He is not only a capable negotiator but also leads the compliance team.
The checklist covers opening the till, reconciling receipts, and locking the safe.
Our partners expect transparency, responsiveness, and that we escalate issues promptly.
To succeed in this market, firms must innovate constantly and listen carefully to customers.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two that-clauses are followed by a bare clause without "that."

Tip: Repeat that before cash was scarce, or drop that before all three.

FALSE — "Not only…but also" joins a noun phrase to a verb phrase.

Tip: Not only a capable negotiator but also the compliance lead — or not only negotiates… but also leads…

TRUE — Three gerund phrases describe procedures in matching form.

Tip: Process lists after "covers" work well as -ing forms.

FALSE — Two nouns are followed by a that-clause.

Tip: Use three nouns: transparency, responsiveness, and prompt escalation.

TRUE — Two bare infinitives after "must" stay parallel.

Tip: Two-item lists still need matching forms after a shared modal.
highlights: not only a capable negotiator but also leads
opening the till, reconciling receipts, and locking
tasks.solution_overview: That-clause series and not only…but also mismatches are classic exam items. Decide whether you are linking nouns or verbs, then refuse any hybrid.

tasks.title: Task 11
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The consultant recommended streamlining processes, automating reports, and that the firm outsource payroll.
As much by design as by accident, the platform became the industry standard.
The keynote was informative, entertaining, and left the audience motivated.
Managers should praise good work publicly and criticise mistakes privately.
The contract prohibits disclosing trade secrets, soliciting clients, and to hire rival staff.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two gerunds are followed by a that-clause.

Tip: Prefer outsourcing payroll so all three recommendations are gerunds.

TRUE — "As much…as" joins two matching "by + noun" phrases.

Tip: Correlative comparisons need identical structures after each as.

FALSE — Two adjectives are followed by a verb phrase.

Tip: Use three adjectives: informative, entertaining, and motivating.

TRUE — Two parallel verb phrases contrast public praise with private criticism.

Tip: Matching adverbs (publicly / privately) reinforce the parallel design.

FALSE — Two gerunds after "prohibits" are followed by an infinitive.

Tip: Use hiring rival staff to keep the gerund series.
highlights: As much by design as by accident
praise good work publicly and criticise
tasks.solution_overview: Legal and advisory prose often piles gerunds after verbs like recommend or prohibit. One infinitive or that-clause at the end will break an otherwise solid series.

tasks.title: Task 12
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The pilot succeeded because of careful scoping, because of clear ownership, and dedicated testers.
She neither confirmed the rumour nor denied it outright.
What the board wants is faster decisions, clearer metrics, and that risks are flagged early.
The new policy applies to permanent staff, to contractors, and interns.
Rather than delaying the launch, the team shipped a limited release and gathered feedback.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two "because of + noun" phrases are followed by a bare noun without "because of."

Tip: Repeat because of before dedicated testers, or drop because of before the first two and use a noun list.

TRUE — "Neither…nor" joins two matching past-tense verbs.

Tip: Keep the same tense and complement pattern after each half.

FALSE — Two noun phrases are followed by a that-clause after "what…is."

Tip: Use three nouns: faster decisions, clearer metrics, and earlier risk flags.

FALSE — "To" appears before the first two groups but not the third.

Tip: Repeat to before interns, or omit to before all three.

TRUE — "Rather than + gerund" is followed by two matching past-tense actions.

Tip: The contrast is with delaying; the main clause then keeps shipped and gathered parallel.
highlights: neither confirmed the rumour nor denied
tasks.solution_overview: Repeated prepositions and correlatives like neither…nor reward careful scanning. If a marker appears twice, check whether the third item still carries it.

tasks.title: Task 13
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The memorandum asks readers to note the assumptions, question the projections, and whether the model is stress-tested.
Both the marketing plan and the sales forecast were updated overnight.
The internship offers mentoring, networking opportunities, and you will receive a stipend.
Investors want founders who can raise capital, who can scale operations, and who can retain talent.
The revision was neither complete nor it was internally consistent.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two infinitives after "asks…to" are followed by a whether-clause.

Tip: Use to check whether the model is stress-tested so the third item stays an infinitive.

TRUE — "Both…and" joins two matching noun subjects with a plural verb.

Tip: Both X and Y take a plural verb when the subjects are plural in sense.

FALSE — Two noun objects are followed by an independent clause.

Tip: Use three nouns: mentoring, networking opportunities, and a stipend.

TRUE — Three matching relative clauses begin with "who can."

Tip: Repeating who can keeps a long relative series clearly parallel.

FALSE — "Neither…nor" joins an adjective to a full clause.

Tip: Neither complete nor internally consistent — two adjectives.
highlights: Both the marketing plan and the sales forecast
who can raise capital, who can scale
tasks.solution_overview: At this level, errors often hide inside long relative or infinitive chains. Isolate the shared frame (asks to… / who can…) and test whether every continuation fits that frame.

tasks.title: Task 14
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The audit found discrepancies in inventory counts, in accounts receivable, and payroll records were incomplete.
Not only the CFO but also the controllers were briefed before the announcement.
We measure success by how quickly we resolve tickets, how rarely issues recur, and customer satisfaction scores.
The brief should explain what changed, why it changed, and how teams should respond.
She is admired for working efficiently, for communicating clearly, and her integrity.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two "in + noun" phrases are followed by an independent clause.

Tip: Keep in payroll records, or rewrite as three noun objects of "in."

TRUE — "Not only…but also" joins two noun subjects; the nearer plural subject takes were.

Tip: Agreement follows the nearer noun after not only…but also.

FALSE — Two "how" clauses are followed by a noun phrase.

Tip: Add how high customer satisfaction scores remain, or turn all three into nouns.

TRUE — Three matching wh-clauses answer what, why, and how.

Tip: Parallel wh-clauses are a strong pattern for instructional briefs.

FALSE — Two "for + gerund" phrases are followed by a bare noun.

Tip: Use for her integrity so every item follows for.
highlights: Not only the CFO but also the controllers
what changed, why it changed, and how
tasks.solution_overview: Wh-clause lists and not only…but also with compound subjects reward precise reading. Do not let a correct agreement pattern distract you from a broken list elsewhere in the set.

tasks.title: Task 15
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The firm’s culture rewards people who take initiative, who share credit, and deliver results without drama.
Either the warranty covers accidental damage or it does not; the brochure cannot claim both.
Objectives for the quarter are reducing churn, increasing average order value, and to reopen two stores.
The mediator asked each side to listen carefully, to summarise the other’s position, and then propose a compromise.
His presentation was organised around three questions: where demand is shifting, which segments are growing, and what pricing can sustain.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two "who" clauses are followed by a bare verb phrase missing "who."

Tip: Write who deliver results without drama to keep the relative pattern.

TRUE — "Either…or" contrasts two matching clauses about coverage.

Tip: Full clauses can be parallel when both sides share the same clause shape.

FALSE — Two gerunds are followed by an infinitive.

Tip: Use reopening two stores to finish the gerund list.

FALSE — Two "to" infinitives are followed by a bare infinitive after "then."

Tip: Write to propose a compromise, or drop to before all three verbs after asked…to.

TRUE — Three matching wh-clauses form a parallel agenda.

Tip: Parallel questions make a presentation structure easy to follow and grammatically clean.
highlights: where demand is shifting, which segments
tasks.solution_overview: Omitted relative pronouns and dropped infinitive markers are easy to miss in long sentences. Mentally restore the shared word before the last item; if it no longer fits, the sentence is false.

tasks.title: Task 16
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The partnership agreement obliges each party to share data promptly, to notify material breaches, and confidentiality must be maintained.
She proved herself both in crisis management and when markets were calm.
The dashboard tracks conversion rates, bounce rates, and how long users stay on the site.
To attract talent, to retain clients, and to protect the brand remain the stated priorities.
The lawyer advised against signing the clause, against waiving notice, and against accepting unlimited liability.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two infinitives are followed by an independent clause with a new modal.

Tip: Use to maintain confidentiality so the obligation stays an infinitive series.

FALSE — "Both…and" joins a prepositional phrase to a when-clause.

Tip: Both in crisis management and in calm markets — two prepositional phrases.

FALSE — Two noun objects are followed by a how-clause.

Tip: Use session duration so all three metrics are noun phrases.

TRUE — Three infinitive phrases function as a parallel compound subject.

Tip: Infinitive subjects can be parallel when every infinitive carries the same role.

TRUE — Three matching "against + gerund" phrases follow "advised."

Tip: Repeating against before each gerund locks the parallel pattern.
highlights: both in crisis management and when
To attract talent, to retain clients, and to protect
against signing the clause, against waiving
tasks.solution_overview: Legal and analytics English mixes nouns, infinitives, and clauses freely in drafts. Your job is to refuse that mixing: pick one frame and hold it through every item.

tasks.title: Task 17
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The turnaround hinged not so much on cutting costs as restoring customer trust through service.
Executives debated whether to refinance the debt, whether to seek an equity partner, or liquidating non-core assets.
The new code of conduct forbids accepting gifts, soliciting favours, and using insider information for personal gain.
Her mandate is as much about rebuilding culture as it is about hitting quarterly targets.
The motion was neither seconded promptly nor was it discussed on the merits.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — "Not so much…as" joins "on cutting" to a bare gerund without "on."

Tip: Not so much on cutting costs as on restoring trust — repeat on.

FALSE — Two "whether to" infinitives are followed by a gerund.

Tip: Or whether to liquidate non-core assets keeps the pattern.

TRUE — Three gerund phrases after "forbids" stay parallel.

Tip: Long gerund objects remain correct when every item is -ing + complement.

TRUE — "As much…as" balances two "about + gerund/noun" ideas with matching "it is."

Tip: Correlative as much…as often needs mirrored about-phrases.

FALSE — "Neither…nor" joins a past participle phrase to an inverted clause.

Tip: Neither seconded promptly nor discussed on the merits — two past participles.
highlights: accepting gifts, soliciting favours, and using
as much about rebuilding culture as it is about
tasks.solution_overview: Advanced correlatives (not so much…as, as much…as, whether to…) fail when the second half drops a preposition or switches to a different verb form. Match the scaffolding, not just the topic.

tasks.title: Task 18
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The prospectus promises investors clearer disclosures, tighter governance, and that dividends will resume within two years.
By training supervisors early, by publishing escalation paths, and by auditing outcomes quarterly, the firm reduced complaints.
The candidate was praised for how she handled objections, how she framed trade-offs, and her closing summary.
We will either migrate the legacy system this year or postpone the project until budgets allow.
The clause requires that vendors deliver on time, that they maintain insurance, and invoices be submitted monthly.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two noun phrases are followed by a that-clause.

Tip: Use resumption of dividends within two years as a third noun phrase.

TRUE — Three matching "by + gerund" phrases form a parallel means list.

Tip: Repeating by before each gerund keeps the causal list balanced.

FALSE — Two "how" clauses are followed by a noun phrase.

Tip: Add how she delivered her closing summary to keep the how-pattern.

TRUE — "Either…or" joins two matching bare infinitives after "will."

Tip: Shared will + either…or needs the same bare verb form on both sides.

FALSE — Two "that" clauses are followed by a bare subjunctive clause missing "that."

Tip: Repeat that before invoices be submitted monthly.
highlights: By training supervisors early, by publishing
either migrate the legacy system this year or postpone
tasks.solution_overview: Prospectus and contract language often stacks that-clauses. If that appears twice, the third clause almost always needs it too—or all three should be rewritten as nouns.

tasks.title: Task 19
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The strategy rests less on aggressive pricing than expanding the service network.
Not only did revenue recover in the second half, but operating margins also widened.
Stakeholders asked for a timeline that is realistic, that is funded, and achievable without overtime.
The committee prefers meeting in person on Mondays and to convene online on Thursdays.
A credible plan must specify who owns each workstream, what resources are required, and when progress will be reviewed.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — "Less…than" joins "on + gerund/noun" to a bare gerund without "on."

Tip: Less on aggressive pricing than on expanding the service network.

TRUE — Inverted "not only" is balanced by "but…also" with a parallel past-tense verb phrase.

Tip: Keep both predicates finite and matching after not only…but also.

FALSE — Two "that is" relatives are followed by an adjective missing "that is."

Tip: Write that is achievable without overtime.

FALSE — A gerund ("meeting") is paired with an infinitive ("to convene").

Tip: Prefer meeting… and convening…, or to meet… and to convene…

TRUE — Three matching wh-clauses specify ownership, resources, and timing.

Tip: Parallel wh-clauses are ideal for plans that must answer who, what, and when.
highlights: who owns each workstream, what resources
tasks.solution_overview: Comparative frames (less…than) and relative-clause chains demand the same marker on every branch. When in doubt, rewrite the last item so it could replace the first without changing structure.

tasks.title: Task 20
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The board authorised management to pursue a sale, to explore a joint venture, and filing for a dual listing if talks stalled.
Just as the firm invests in product research, so too does it invest in after-sales support.
Performance will be judged on whether targets are met, whether risks are logged, and staff development plans exist.
The brief is neither to defend the status quo nor to dismiss every criticism wholesale.
She left the firm because of limited promotion prospects, because of a toxic team culture, and her commute had become unmanageable.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Two infinitives after "authorised…to" are followed by a gerund.

Tip: Use to file for a dual listing to keep the infinitive series.

TRUE — "Just as…so too" balances two matching invest + in + noun patterns with inversion on the second clause.

Tip: Correlative just as…so too needs mirrored clause structure.

FALSE — Two "whether" clauses are followed by a bare clause missing "whether."

Tip: Repeat whether before staff development plans exist.

TRUE — "Neither…nor" joins two matching infinitives after "is."

Tip: Keep to + bare verb on both sides of neither…nor.

FALSE — Two "because of + noun" phrases are followed by an independent clause.

Tip: Use because of an unmanageable commute so every reason stays a noun phrase.
highlights: and filing for a dual listing
neither to defend the status quo nor to dismiss
tasks.solution_overview: Final-band items combine correlatives, repeated subordinators, and long infinitive chains. Name the opening structure of each sentence, then reject any ending that cannot wear the same grammatical clothes.
